rows.what the ink shows: Two separate dark dots lie one above the other after Applications; there is no connected oval body or grave-accented a.

The opening p has a long descending loop joined at the baseline. The following two compact upper remnants are intersected by the heavy horizontal deletion, so their o/s bodies are not independently recoverable.

The large opening symbol is rounded and retraced, with a raised parenthesized glyph and a separate dotted lower stem followed by angled index strokes. Cancellation merges the main crossing and several lower joins; the complete sum/lambda/E sequence or tensor-and-index sequence cannot be distinguished securely.

An initial tall b and low rounded trace survive; the next word has a low opening arch, paired tall middle stems and a later upright, and the final group retains a tall opening and terminal t. The deletion runs through the intervening letter bodies, preventing secure recovery of the full words.

Below the insertion enclosure, a short opening stroke, a broad low loop, a later upright with rightward foot and a detached small upper stroke remain. The horizontal deletion merges the upper bodies and punctuation, so the proposed s'obtient cannot be read throughout.
The entire short body is overwritten by a dense triangular black patch, leaving only small upper gaps and a right drooping stroke. At sixfold enlargement no distinct baseline letter sequence remains.
A short left upright and a right terminal hook remain inside two heavy oblique/horizontal cancellation strokes. The middle oval and u-shaped bodies required to distinguish tout are covered.
Three separated groups are visible: a low linked opening group, a separate rounded a, and the joined low strokes of un. The separate middle a and absence of a tall t favor on a un over est un.

The opening word has a tall crossed stroke and a detached acute at its right; the following low connected sequence ends before a separate broad curled sigma. The visible spacing and strokes support noté encore followed by the symbol.

Short uprights and a descending loop survive around the thick cancellation rule, but it covers the connected middle bodies needed to verify isomorphisme. Magnification and contrast do not expose a distinguishing word outline.
The crossed continuation retains a low wavering stroke, an isolated downstroke, and a dark terminal knot beneath the cancellation. These surviving fragments do not identify the two erased words.

Above the tensor symbol there is a short separate left stroke and a compact tall hooked body with a rightward curve. The first stroke could be an opening parenthesis, but the central shape and closing curve do not separate cleanly enough to distinguish (2) from n, even beside the clear same-page (2).

A tall upright near the beginning and a shorter upright near the end survive the heavy diagonal-to-horizontal deletion. The intervening small letter bodies are merged into that rule, so they do not independently establish autre.

Before the separate les, the short word has an open rising initial s-hook followed by a low joined u movement and a flattened terminal r exit. Its middle is compressed, but the visible sequence supports sur.

An opening parenthesis precedes the long commutativité group with low joined m/u bodies and several projecting t strokes. The separate du and produit groups, tall initial of tensoriel, h/l uprights of hilbertien, and final closing parenthesis remain visible despite crowding beneath the formula.

A heavy horizontal cancellation covers almost the whole short form; only a small initial upright, a detached dot and a downward loop near the middle survive. These do not independently establish the numeral or the complete suffix.

Between pour and i, the cancelled group is reduced to a dark left angular upright, converging diagonal strokes and a short final upward hook. The original interior letter bodies are hidden, so tout remains unconfirmed.

The cancelled capital retains a pointed apex, separate sloping legs and a transverse middle bar, with a small triangular opening above the bar. These distinguish A despite the additional crossing stroke.

A rounded upper enclosure survives between the norm factors, but heavy crossing strokes fill its lower half. Unlike the clear earlier circled crosses on this same formula line, the target does not preserve two independently distinguishable diagonals.
